utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Micic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Yesterday, I said I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Today my language is a bit different. Today, under Rule 91(A), the Chamber, proprio motu, warns you of your duty to tell the truth and confronts you with the possible consequences of not speaking the truth. That is a maximum penalty a fine of 100.000 euros or a term of imprisonment of seven years. That can be the consequences of failing to fulfil that duty. I add to that, and that's perhaps far more important, that if a witness extensively testifies and if some of his answers could give the impression that they are not in accordance with a duty of a witness to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but truth, that perhaps the remainder of his testimony might not receive the credit it perhaps deserves, which could be detrimental for the party who called that witness; in this case the Defence. So this is a formal warning under Rule 91. I add to that, Mr. Tieger, that the Chamber could imagine circumstances in which a cross-examining party would refrain from spending much time going into all kind of details when it challenges the credibility and reliability of a witness. So the Chamber could imagine circumstances in which the cross-examining party would choose a global approach and would consider that would be sufficient. Of course it's left to the party, but the Chamber could understand that under certain circumstances one would not go -- would not pay a lot of attention, a lot of time to all details if a global impression has been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I simply observe that since Your Honour was going through the technical formality of warning the witness as to the consequences, the two possible consequences that Your Honour indicated, there is a further possibility that it can, strictly speaking, be both, and I wonder whether Your Honour should, for absolute completeness, make --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree that Rule 91(G) says both. So Mr. Stewart corrects me adequately - very adequately - to say that it's not only 100.000 euros or a term of imprisonment of seven years but there is the possibility that both penalties could be imposed if it would be established that a false testimony under solemn declaration is given. Mr. Tieger, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Micic. I expect to be --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I expect to be quite brief this afternoon, as I've already advised my learned colleagues from the Defence, so my questions for you and this phase of your examination should be short, especially if you can answer any questions that I put to you that may be answered appropriately with a yes or no with simply a yes or no. You testified yesterday and the day before about the activities of Arkan and about support by Mrs. Plavsic for Arkan, and then you were asked, at page 30 of yesterday's LiveNote, whether you were ever aware of any support given by Mr. Krajisnik for the activities of Arkan, and your response was, "No. As far as I know, the only support that Arkan enjoyed was from Mrs. Plavsic." Were you aware, Mr. Micic, at any time of Mr. Krajisnik offering praise or expressing some form of praise for Arkan's positive and significant efforts, or indicating that he should have -- that he had positive and significant credits when it comes to the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether any such things happened. Probably, if Arkan was there, and I assume he was, but I really don't remember anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me show you a brief video clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I'd ask that that be marked next in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, did we assign already a number to yesterday's video clip?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P1022, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's for yesterday's.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for today's video.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be P1023.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. By the way, Mr. Tieger, have you verified yesterday whether or not this 34th session was already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there may be some confusion. I actually checked to see whether an excerpt from the 46th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 46th. I might make a mistake here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the Court was quite correct; that is P529, Hanson tab 468, and that is the entirety of that session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that number then will -- perhaps to avoid whatever confusion, we leave that number open so that we have no -- we don't have a subsequent numbering, but otherwise having two documents under one number ever would certainly create all kind of confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I quite agree, and in that connection it's important for me to note that the document that was given P1021 was the previous exhibit, and I think that's P653.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll try to sort that out with the registrar so that we don't have any doubles. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps before it's played, we could be handed out the -- what I think are the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Anchor: Viewer from Sid asked

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: What do you think about Arkan's statement regarding acts of deputies of Republika Srpska and at all-Serbian Assembly and at the previous Assembly? "Momcilo Krajisnik: I think that Mr. Arkan has many positive and significant credits when it comes to the Serbian people. So when I consider his negative statements, the balance is still positive. So I do not blame him. Nobody banned deputies to come to the Parliament. Every deputy can confirm that. We simply have deputy and assembly discipline. Discipline to respect each other. And I am grateful to deputies for accepting an appeal not to attend this Assembly session without any pressure at all because it was the conclusion of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party and our Assembly."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First, Mr. Micic, do you recall seeing that particular broadcast before?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is some television programme. I think it was a programme from Pale. I recognise this anchor. But I don't remember the programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And does seeing this broadcast jog your memory about any other occasions on which you heard or became aware of Mr. Krajisnik expressing his views about the many positive and significant credits that Arkan had with respect to the Serbian people, or any other praise along those lines?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember. You must understand that that was, after all, some 12 or 13 years ago, and I am of an age where I cannot remember everything very well. Now, as for Arkan himself, I considered him to be very bad and very negative, and I always did my best not to be in the same room that he was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention now to the period of time before the walkout of the SDS deputies at the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, could you give us, as always, some context as far as time is concerned of this -- of this video, of this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I will endeavour to do so, Your Honour. I'm reasonably confident that there are a number of contextual --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but please provide --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- facts that will permit us to do so within appropriate limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, I had just asked you to turn your attention back to the period of time before the walkout of the SDS at the joint Bosnian Assembly on October 14th or 15th, 1991. Before that time, in let's say September, mid-September, mid to late September 1991, based on your contact with Mr. Krajisnik or Dr. Karadzic, were they aware that you could be counted on to support SDS policies? That is, did you indicate to them that they -- that you could be counted on to support SDS policies?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think they could count on that in view of the overall SDS policies, but when there was out-voting, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the most significant issues of concern to the Bosnian Serb leadership and the SDS, that is those matters for which out-voting was a subject of concern, did you make clear to Mr. Krajisnik or Dr. Karadzic that they could count on you for support; in essence, that you were their man?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I attended on one occasion in the deputies' club of the SDS. I was there once, I know that I just addressed them, or not, but I left the meeting. I don't really remember. But that I discussed the matter openly, that I would listen to them to the letter, I don't think there was anything like that. And I don't think they made such demands upon me, because they had an absolute majority. So several of us independent deputies in the Assembly later on didn't represent a real force in the Assembly of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me have marked the next exhibit in order, that's found at tab 16, it's an intercepted conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik of September 18, 1991. I appreciate that the current state of numbering makes it a bit difficult for the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just learned from the registrar that, as far as the previous exhibits are concerned, they're now renumbered, that the video clip that is the television broadcast with Mr. Micic and Mr. Maksimovic would be P1020, so the transcript then being 1020A, A.1 for the English translation. And the video we just looked at, which was the footage in which Mr. Krajisnik appears, would be P1021, and then A for the transcript and A.1 for the English translation. Apart from that, since we're dealing with it anyway, Mr. Tieger, perhaps it would be a good idea to limit P1020 to the portion that was actually played, because we are now in the possession of a copy which contains other portions of the video which we haven't seen, unless you'd like to tender that as a kind of contextual written exhibit. Then, of course, we should hear from the Defence whether there would be any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That would be my intention, Your Honour. I think the Defence had a chance to see it. I certainly want to give them ample opportunity to look at it in the context the Court mentions, but I don't anticipate any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We would want that opportunity, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then at least I do not invite to you provide the Chamber at this moment with a shorter version of P1020. Please proceed. We have now the last number to be assigned. That is the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1023, Your Honours -- 22. 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would then be the intercepted telephone conversation. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Micic, as I indicated, the document that you're now looking at is a transcript of a conversation between Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik on September 18, 1991. And if you can -- would begin at the portion of the conversation about roughly halfway down the first page, Mr. Krajisnik says: "Well, I can tell you, I've just been over to ... have a talk with the reformists." Dr. Karadzic says: "Uh-huh. "Mr. Krajisnik: I've had no success with you so they seem to have ... you know, there are many possibilities for you to improve, you're successful. "Dr. Karadzic: Uh-huh, yes. "Mr. Krajisnik: You can't fix anything there anymore. "Dr. Karadzic: All right. Who is this ...? "Mr. Krajisnik: Our man, Momcilo Micic from Tuzla. "Dr. Karadzic: Uh-huh. "Mr. Krajisnik: He's ours, you know, he's got a brother here." Mr. Micic, do you recall the specific details of the conversation you and the other reformists had with Mr. Krajisnik on September 18, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion I did go to see Mr. Krajisnik in his offices, and I think Dragan Kalinic was with me on the occasion, and perhaps someone else, I don't know, but I think we went there with respect to a request from the party, the Reformist Party alliance with respect to the Assembly, because we'd already left the alliance of reformist parties. That's how I came to be there. Now, what he said, who he talked to, what his assessments and evaluations were I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I take it from your answer, sir, that you don't recall the specific conversation that Mr. Krajisnik is referring to in this conversation. I heard you say "yes" but I don't see it -- I didn't hear an answer from the interpreter's booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was your answer yes, Mr. Micic? Yes in the sense that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Whatever the details of that conversation, however, Mr. Micic, can we agree that you left Mr. Krajisnik in no doubt that you were their man; that is, Dr. Karadzic's and Mr. Krajisnik's man?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't do anything to leave that impression, but if they did have that impression, I can't know that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have nothing further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. Mr. Stewart, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you wanted to address the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, before Mr. Krajisnik begins, can we inquire whether he will be raising any matter that requires the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could first briefly tell us what you would like to say. May I just ask you, would you want to ask any additional questions to the witness, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I would like to ask questions based on the questions by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then as usual you are first expected to consult with counsel before I will give you an opportunity to do so. Perhaps with the assistance of Mr. Karganovic you could, unless you are aware already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: May I make a preliminary inquiry first, Your Honour, and then if it suggests that I need more time, then I'll say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. Please do so, and take care that all the microphones are off.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's quite clear - and I see Mr. Krajisnik has some notes - I have to ask for a few minutes to consult him properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn for -- for a start, seven minutes. Would that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: From the note, Your Honour, maybe ten minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ten minutes. Okay. We'll adjourn until 3.00. --- Break taken at 2.50 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you for that opportunity. My position as counsel is still that the Defence would have no re-examination. That's full stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear, and as we decided before, if Mr. Krajisnik thinks that additional questions should be put to the witness, that in view of his wish to be actively involved in his -- in his Defence, the Chamber will not disallow him to put some additional questions if he insists on doing it after having sought advice from his counsel. Mr. Krajisnik, the Chamber at the same time, I would say especially now under the present circumstances, will insist on proper formulation of questions. That is, this is your witness, so you should not lead the witness. So you may put some additional questions to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you saw the footage when Krajisnik said about Arkan, "I think that Mr. Arkan has many positive and significant credits when it comes to the Serbian people. So when I consider his negative statements, the balance is still positive," and so on and so forth. My question is: Was the point to commend Arkan, or was the point to tell the deputies who did not go to the -- deputies who did not go to the Assembly to talk about Arkan. Maybe we can look at the footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Tieger, that by this question the witness is invited to comment on what the speaker had in mind. From what I understand is that the speaker will testify soon. What we could ask the witness - and let me take over, Mr. Krajisnik - have you seen this footage at that time? I think you testified that you did not; is that correct? Or that you have no recollection of having seen it at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I do not recall seeing it, and I don't think that I did see it. That programme was broadcast from Studio Pale, whereas I was living in Belgrade and in Belgrade it wasn't possible to see those programmes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, having seen this footage, is there -- does there come anything in your mind which would assist the Chamber to better understand this footage and what matter actually was addressed when Mr. Krajisnik spoke these words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would perhaps interpret that a little differently. Arkan did enjoy certain -- not honours but confidence and sympathies from a certain number of people in Republika Srpska also, and I think that other than what Mr. Krajisnik said, that this was also addressed to the viewers in some way not to create a bad atmosphere in Republika Srpska itself, but it was probably also said with the intention that somebody else hears it too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that what comes into your mind? Mr. Krajisnik, it appears that you are the speaker. If your counsel would like to know exactly what was addressed by you at that time, I take it that -- and since you have an opportunity to consult counsel before testifying, and that questions, if they would assist the Chamber, will certainly be put to you and we would hear your answer. We now heard from the witness what he -- what came into his mind and what would assist the Chamber in better understanding the video clip. Please proceed with your next question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like for His Honour to formulate the question that I wanted to put to the witness, because the text here is much longer. It includes more besides what is said about Arkan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a bit -- I formulated your last question in such a way that it was, I hope, not objectionable any more by the Prosecution, but if it is about the interpretation and the gist of what was said in this television programme, Mr. Krajisnik, if it's about that, I already told you that you'll have an ample opportunity, first of all, to consult with counsel and then to answer any question in relation to that when you testify yourself. We have now heard from the witness what comes into his mind now seeing this footage which he hasn't seen at that time. So please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: The next question, Mr. Micic, is: You have been accused here of not speaking the truth because you could not recall ever hearing about strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, no one is accused. This witness is warned. You should carefully listen to what we say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Warned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's more or less -- it's more or less commenting. This Chamber is fully aware that the witness has told us that on the -- on the subject of the six strategic goals what his recollection is and was. The witness has been warned. If there is any question to put to the witness, could you do that without these kind of introductions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may put the question, Your Honour, please permit me to do that. If not, well, then I really cannot concentrate because of your interruptions. I just wanted to make an introduction and then put the question to the witness. You didn't accuse the witness, but the Prosecutor accused him yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Put the question to the witness without these kind of introductions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were given the example that you could not recall the strategic goals from the meeting of August and September 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to have that material in front of him so that he can follow. 0215-0513. Actually, 508. That is the minutes of the recording of the 34th session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could tab 7 be put in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the corresponding English portion, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that you say, Mr. Krajisnik, 508. That's the cover page; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Right. Now, which page you especially wanted to address the witness's attention to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two pages. That's the fifth page, 0215-0513.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you found that? That's page 5 of the -- page 5 of the document. And, Mr. Tieger, for your information, that is page 6 of the English. At least, I think it is. That's the agenda, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you please read item 2 of this agenda.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Constitutional agreement on the Alliance of the BiH Republics."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this debate was conducted as part of this item of the agenda?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say that the question is not leading, Mr. Krajisnik, but perhaps I can imagine -- I take it that you want to draw our attention to the fact that the remarks -- some of the remarks the witness was confronted with were made when agenda item 2 was discussed. Mr. Tieger, I take it that we could proceed. Yes. Next question, please, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have a map placed on the ELMO so the witness could look at it, and that's the agreement that was actually being adopted at that session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any exhibit? Oh, you have a -- is that already in evidence? And perhaps you also showed --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think that it's already been admitted. I think the best thing would be for it to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if we place it on the ELMO, we'll try to track that down to the exhibit number it represents. It is on the ELMO. Could we zoom in a bit because the light is -- do you want to look at the left-hand side or the right-hand side, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both sides, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Light is a bit of a problem. Is there any way of adjusting that? Yes, that's better. Mr. Krajisnik, you may put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like you to read the titles or the caption under the first map and under the second map. I'm now addressing the witness.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you read it allowed, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Owen's Balkan --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: No, underneath the map.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Underneath the map, map 9, it says: "The union of three republics, August 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: And what about the caption beneath the second map?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Map 10, areas from which according to the union map Serbs should withdraw in 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: My question is: Do you remember the discussion about that plan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I'd first like to have the map again on the -- on our screens so that we can better look at it. Yes. There we are again. Yes. Your question -- the question put to you, Mr. Micic, was whether you remember the discussion about that plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do remember the discussions, but we would need to have more time, or I would need to have more information in order to be able to recall better this exact discussion. I think this is Cutileiro's map, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Well, take as much time as you need.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really remember anything more specific. I do remember that there were always some maps on the board and that there was discussion about this and how the Serbs did not want to withdraw, especially not from this part called Visoko Krajina, and here it is said that they were supposed to withdraw from there, and I think the largest number of questions were about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Very well. So you don't recall. Can we conclude that you do not recall the discussion about these maps and this plan from 1993, from August 1993?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can conclude really that I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Now, I would like to look at 7.A and B -- no, I'm actually talking about tab 7.A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Krajisnik, what is in evidence - that's D61.1 - is some pages of the B/C/S -- it's D61, some pages of the book by David Owen, "Balkan Odyssey," and we have D61.1, the translation of these same pages. The maps that appear both in the B/C/S original and in the English translation are, first of all, only maps which look similar and, as a matter of fact, two copies, two maps which look more or less similar as compared to the one on page 246 of the document you have asked us to put on the ELMO. It looks as if there are two different versions of the book in B/C/S, the B/C/S version, because the pages that are in evidence - that's D61 - are 266 and 267 and 312, 313, whereas the maps here appear on 246 and 247, and 246 very much resembles the map on page 266 of the copy that is in evidence that's D61, but is not exactly the same. So therefore we'll verify, perhaps, but it's not exactly the same. It's not in evidence. So I'd like Mr. Registrar to assign a D number to the maps which we find now on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D114, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that's for pages bearing 246 and 247.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Micic, your attention is drawn to tab 7.A. Would you please look at tab 7.A. And, Mr. Krajisnik, would you please put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: On page 25 -- actually 0215-0643 --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Well, let's just check whether Their Honours and my friends from the Prosecution have found the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have. 7.A, page 128 in the English is the first page of 7.A.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: It says there "Presiding," and then strategic goals are discussed. I would like you to tell us who the presiding person was.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On page 28, 0215-0646, you can see there the way voting was conducted. I would just like to help you find it.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, it's page 131 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Could you please read the part after the voting and before the applause, the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I would like to ask you to return to our work. We need to adopt the platform now."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: What -- it's the first paragraph above that, where it says: "Who is in favour? "Who is opposed? "Who abstains ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Gentlemen, you have got Republic of Srpska!"

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's just see if Their Honours have found that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we've found it. We followed it. It's the part that starts with --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Gentlemen, you have got Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were shown the decision on the establishment of the Serb municipality of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: You were faced with the presentation of Mr. Milan Tesic, and that is 0214-9623. I do apologise but it was a separate document. It wasn't in the binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you retrieve that document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is number 17, with the decision on the founding of the Serbian municipality of Tuzla, the Tuzla municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was in the binder. Tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you see the heading there and the date when the meeting was held? It says "Decision on the establishment," et cetera. What date was that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have two dates in the preamble.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Read out what it says. "At a meeting held ..." when?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian municipality of Tuzla is being established. "The Serbian municipality is hereby established. The municipality's seat is in Tuzla. The territory --" et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: No. In the heading, before the title "Decision."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Pursuant to Article 116 of the Constitution of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, SFRY, Official Gazette -" et cetera - "Article 2 on the territories of municipalities, local communes and settlements in Bosnia and Herzegovina which are considered to be the territory of the Federal State of Yugoslavia of the 21st of November, 1992, and Article 4 of the Instructions on the organisation and activity of organs of the Serbian people in BH under emergency circumstances of the 19th of December, 1991, the Assembly of the Serbian municipality of Tuzla adopted, as its session held on the 3rd of March, 1992, the following "Decision..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Yes. So the date is the 3rd of March. Now, I would like to ask you to take a look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, the interpreters have translated the 21st of November, 1992, which actually does appear in the English version, but the original says 21st of February, 1991. So that should be corrected. And I take it that the interpreters, looking at the original, would agree with me. I don't know what the witness read, whether he read 1991 or 1992 but it seems obvious --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter said what she heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: If I might just point out Your Honour, I think inadvertently, said February there as well, or that's what appears in the transcript, which is going to add to the difficulty clearing up this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the date the 21st of November. I now do understand from the interpreters that the witness read 21st of November, 1992, although the original in B/C/S says 1991, and the English, I think, incorrectly translates this into 1992. But we are focusing now, Mr. Micic, on the adoption of this decision on the 3rd of March, 1992. Please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were shown the discussion by Mr. Milan Tesic. 0214-9623 was the number.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same tab?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: No, it was a separate document, a separate piece of paper. It says tape number 28. It's not in the binder. But anyway, you were presented with the discussion that Mr. Tesic had at the Assembly, what he said. The number is 4-9623, the last few digits. I can provide you with my own copy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness can take my copy because I know what it's about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we could put the original on the ELMO for the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Could you put it up a bit. Would you read out three lines of what Mr. Tesic says.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said: "Ladies and gentlemen, distinguished persons, we brought in the decision to form the Tuzla municipality on the 23rd of March. It was sent by telefax on the 24th of March, and here we have the trace of the telex. So by omission, the decision was not verified and introduced into the already verified municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. May we then conclude that the date of the decision is different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you don't know how to put these questions to the witness, but I'll try to do as good as I can to raise the issue. Mr. Micic, the document you were just shown, tab 17, gives the 3rd of March, 1992, as the date on which the decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Tuzla was adopted. In the passage you just read, the adoption, because there was a slight problem with the translation and it was corrected, the date of the adoption of the decision on establishing the Tuzla municipality is 23rd of March. Could you give us any explanation as to the difference in dates we can observe in these two documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he says here that he has a telex with that date, when it was dispatched, the fax. So quite obviously there is a collision between the two. Now, I'd like to return you to what I -- to take you back to what I said the day before yesterday. I don't know that the Serbian municipality of Tuzla was established and that there was an attempt to form it in another place, not in Tuzla. So this is pressure exerted, consistently exerted by Milan Tesic and a Professor named Professor Stavic who insisted that I should prevail with the Assembly organs to verify the municipality and give it legality. And they said to me that if the municipality was not verified, then I would lose my term of office, my mandate. And I said right, fine, then it will never be verified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were aware of any decision that needed verification at that time and decision which in your view was not fully correct, but you were sent with this message by, you said, Professor -- on the record it says that pressure was exerted by Milan Tesic and Professor Stavic, it says, that it should be -- it should go to the Assembly organs to verify that. That's what you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but that was much later than this date. That pressure was exerted much later, when the Serbs had already started leaving Tuzla. And I said that before this Trial Chamber. So that was when the municipalities were formed and established in Bijeljina -- in Lopare first and then in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say much later, would that still be within the -- within the time frame running from the 3rd of March to the 23rd, or would that be outside that period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Much later. After May. Perhaps even July/August 1992. And all -- I can just interpret this. It's my free interpretation that it was machination on the part of Tesic to convince the Assembly that something had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik. Put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were shown a document sent by Petar Jankovic to Minister Ostojic. The number is 00017, the last digits. Shall we just take a moment for everybody to be able to find it? It was a handwritten document.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's tab 18, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. I apologise, Your Honour. Yes, tab 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I was informed that that document was already in evidence, so the number assigned to it yesterday is withdrawn. So we are now at tab 18. Yes, please, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Just the first page. Can you see a date there in the upper left-hand column, upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the 25th of March, 1992. You mean the stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 23rd of March, 1992, is that the one you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at the signature at the end there, at the end of the document on the second page. Can you read out what it says. Who signed?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Serbian municipality of Kalesija, Petar Jankovic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Now, Kalesija, is that within the region of Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Does that confirm your statement to the effect that there were attempts to form municipalities outside Tuzla and that Tuzla hadn't formed its Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question now. You spoke about a meeting yesterday with Mr. Savo Jankovic and Mr. Karadzic, Krajisnik, in the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us, please, who scheduled the meeting? Who told you to go to a meeting like that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was you. I called you, and I think you scheduled the meeting. And you were the only person that I could contact. I couldn't contact anybody from the government or the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I will remind the Trial Chamber that you said yesterday that you were disillusioned because you received no plans or, to put it in a better way, you never heard of any plan from Mr. Karadzic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I'd like to ask the Trial Chamber to take a look at the following: It is the Assembly held on the 27th of March, 1992. 025873 is the number of the document. We had it yesterday. That's the page number, the last four digits 5873.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That very much seems to be under tab 4. Is that correct, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. I think I have a different set of tabs, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have -- as a matter of fact, the 27th of March would have been the 14th Assembly. Is that -- I have that under tab 4, but it does not give the number you just indicated. Let me just check.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but I have a copy here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please say the numbers slower. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slowly read again the ERN number, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] SA025873.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some difficulty in finding that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 31 of the Serbian transcript, if that could be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which tab, then, for you, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, I received a separate set of documents from the session of the 27th of March, and the Prosecutor did mention that particular session himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, is there any way you could assist us, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think -- in one sense, Your Honour, I think there are extracts from the 14th session but not the entirety of the 14th session copied and provided in that tab. So if Mr. Krajisnik is referring to a portion of the Assembly session that was not contained in that particular tab, none of us have it but him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, yes. Thank you for your assistance, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Krajisnik, do you have the B/C/S version available so that we could put it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly, with the greatest of pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please assist Mr. Krajisnik. If portions are read, could it be done slowly so that the interpreters can follow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to say that this is what Mr. Karadzic said, and you can check that out in the minutes from the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the portion you would like to draw the attention of the witness to be read, could you please invite the witness to read it, but then slowly, and also to indicate exactly what portion you would like him to read. Is it the highlighted portion, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask the witness to read the highlighted portion, because it is Prosecution material, and I did mark the extract I wanted him to read. The lower part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The war in Bosnia-Herzegovina will not solve anything, but if it does start, they will receive the plans, but could you place the people in the formation of the Territorial Defence straight away, put reserve officers at their head so that units and companies should be formed as well as Crisis Staffs and pensioned officers should be engaged and involved as well. This should be done in the whole of our area. "In the Crisis Staff we have the president of the municipality, the Executive Board, the highest people in our authorities, plus the reserve officers and the situation for defence of lives and property should be studied as well as territory. We have no other plans."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that confirm your observation that Mr. Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have to object to questions that begin, "Can we conclude ..." "Does that confirm ..." et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you can put questions to the witness but not ask for a conclusion and then formulate yourself what the conclusion should be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll reformulate that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: The text you read out, is that different from your conclusion from the meeting with Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does differ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what way?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here that some steps were taken as to how that should be done, whereas at the meeting we didn't gain that impression and we didn't receive information of that kind. As far as I recall his statement, he said the people will decide for themselves. Now, the people, when he said the people, I didn't know what he meant, so I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Perhaps I wasn't precise enough in asking my question. All I want to ask you is this, and it has to do with the plans: He says, "We don't have any other plans." That's the last sentence, and I'm asking you whether that part of the sentence, or excerpt, differs or coincides with the impression you yourself gained when you visited Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't differ.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krajisnik. Let's see whether the Bench has any questions to Mr. Micic. Mr. Micic, Judge Hanoteau has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have a technical question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's better - Judge Hanoteau has one or more questions for you, I have one or more questions four as well - to first have a break. We will adjourn until quarter past four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I would like to announce to the parties that, as I indicated before, that the Chamber was considering to sit tomorrow the whole of the day, that we have decided that we would -- that we will. We have received no responses or objections to it. And then Friday is still uncertain. Yes, Judge Hanoteau would have some questions for you, Mr. Micic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a couple of questions for the witness. The first one is on the institutional relationship. You talked about the two assemblies; one, the people's Assembly, and other one is the municipal -- the Assembly of municipalities, to put things simply.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could you tell me who was chairing these two Assemblies. Was there a single chairperson for the two Assemblies or did each Assembly have a president?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me for what period of time you're thinking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm talking about the period before Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the establishment of Republika Srpska, the Assembly, the people's Assembly or, rather, the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Assembly, was just one Assembly with two houses. The president of that Assembly was Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik. And every municipality had its own Assembly and its own president.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. But this Assembly had two Chambers, is that it? One is the Council of Peoples, and the other one was the Council of Municipalities. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these two councils, were they always chaired by Mr. Krajisnik even when they were sitting separately?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When the Chamber of Citizens met, it was Dr. Konjicija that presided, and the Assembly of Municipalities was Petko Cancar. If Momcilo Krajisnik happened to be at any of those Assemblies, he would attend just like any other deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krajisnik was chairing the plenary sessions when the two Assemblies were together. Then it was Mr. Krajisnik that was presiding. Is that it? Is that the way it worked?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the way it worked. Thank you. Thank you for this. A second question now about what you called the massacre of May 15th. Was this an isolated event in your municipality or were there already similar events? And I'm talking about incidents, you know, where Muslims were committing -- were against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first incidents -- that was the first incident on that territory. Before that, there were no incidents of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And after May 15th were there other incidents of the same kind? Serious incidents I'm talking about, serious incidents, or was it really an isolated event?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 15th of May, the Yugoslav People's Army withdrew its forces and equipment from the airport at Dubrava, near Tuzla, and that's when an entire column left through Tuzla, but nothing happened, because there were threats by the then colonel, the commander of the airport, of the air field, that he would blow up the planes. And I think two or three MiGs were flying over Tuzla at that time. I wasn't in Tuzla myself, but that's the information I received. So that column passed through quite quietly, without any incidents taking place. They left Tuzla that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can go a little bit further into this. Were there aggressions carried out by the Muslims against the Serbs that had stayed in Tuzla? Murders, slaughters, or nothing? And I'm talking about that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you give me details?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were certain groups of armed people who had their private prisons, and there was abuse, mistreatment, killings and attempts of people leaving Tuzla by a roundabout route, or where there weren't any roads. There was shooting. Those people was shot at, and some were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But you haven't witnessed anything because you weren't there. You heard about this; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I wasn't, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you heard about this only.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you as well. Mr. Krajisnik asked you a question about who arranged for the meeting you had with Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik early in 1992. The month of March was mentioned. You said that you called him because you could not call anyone from the Presidency. Nevertheless, Mr. Karadzic was present. Could you explain what happened that made Mr. Karadzic to be present. Did you ask for it? Was it offered to you? How was this all arranged, this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I asked for a meeting with Mr. Karadzic. I asked Mr. Krajisnik to arrange for a meeting with Mr. Karadzic for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you then specifically ask Mr. Krajisnik to be present as well or were you just seeking a meeting with Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't specific. I don't think I put any conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, when you -- why did you call Mr. Krajisnik if you wanted to have a meeting with Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the simple reason to come into connection with Mr. Karadzic. I don't know otherwise where I could have found him, come into contact with him, because he was just a party president at that time. He wasn't a functionary, he wasn't in the Presidency of Bosnia or in its Assembly either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wouldn't that make it even easier to contact him directly when he had no function?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would probably have to do that via the local SDS, but I didn't want to even attempt to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Totally different subject: You told us how quite a substantive load of oil was stolen, as far as I understand, or at least seized by Mauzer. You remember your testimony about that?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that you heard that it was Mauzer, if I -- if my recollection is correct, through your brother who was in the Crisis Staff with Mauzer. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I had, the Crisis Staff that issued orders and left written documents about that, and in the Crisis Staff that that should be that way is something that was done, or even if you want, ordered by Mauzer himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And your brother was a member of that Crisis Staff as well?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he remain on that Crisis Staff for how long?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He remained there, but for how long I don't really know. Until the establishment of the legal government. I can't tell you exactly when that was but, yes, he did remain for some time. I think that there were seven or eight of them, perhaps nine, I don't know how many in the staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If I may say, the witness didn't in fact himself say anything specific but the question that Your Honour put a few moments ago when -- it's on the transcript, "... if my recollection --" "You've told us that you heard that it was Mauzer, if I -- if my recollection is correct, through your brother who was in the Crisis Staff with Mauzer," and the thrust of Your Honour's questions is that both the witness's brother and Mauzer were on the Crisis Staff. I don't know whether that was what Your Honour intended to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was intended to say and at the same time I'm now checking the transcript whether I may have made a mistake. That's why I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's the question I'm raising, Your Honour, with respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could assist me. If you would have exactly -- I'm approximately at page 23, 24 of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm there or thereabouts, Your Honour. It could be my transcript started at a different point. Does Your Honour have a phrase that I could find?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What I have is -- and therefore I might not have been fully certain. You testified yesterday, "He told me that he was with them in this SDS committee."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I have that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was -- so it was not on the Crisis Staff but on the committee. And then you said, "Mauzer became the master of Bijeljina." So please forget about whether they were on the Crisis Staff together or not, but they were in relation with each other. They had -- they had contacts, and from what I understand they were on -- together on a committee. When you said "Mauzer became the master of Bijeljina," could you explain to us a bit more in detail what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time he had a military formation under him, but I don't know how he managed to get that military formation. So he had the only armed personnel. He deployed them. He was the one who decided about everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So he had a military formation. He expressed his wish to kill you, from what I understand. Did you ever ask your brother why he worked with a man who took this position and had this bad intention?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that they cooperated. I thought that they were in some committee. I don't know if Mauzer was elected by somebody to the committee or was he co-opted. I don't know. He probably attended all of these meetings, and there was a debate conducted at the Assembly. When I was discussed, it was said that I had inflicted a lot of harm or damage on the Serbian people and that I was supposed to pay with my life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. You told us that you had a meeting or meetings in Belgrade where you sought assistance. You were talking about food, about clothing. When did you have that meeting in Belgrade, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was after the 15th of May, 1992. It could have been in the fall or in the summer of 1992. Winter was coming, and we needed to provide for these people. So all of that was asked for. There were a lot of pressures from the refugees on the local population who couldn't take that any more. There was this collective accommodation. It was full. There had to be a way to put these people up somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. With whom did you meet in Belgrade, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean of the Belgrade officials or those who had come from the Tuzla municipality or from the Tuzla area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The ones from Belgrade you met with.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in touch with the Government of Republika Srpska, with its Ministry for Serbs Outside of Serbia, and with a minister of theirs, a certain Mr. Djuretic, who then referred to me to the Red Cross of the Republic of Serbia or Federal Yugoslavia, or Yugoslavia at the time, and we received assistance from the Red Cross. I don't know where the Red Cross received this aid from. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Micic, I have no further questions for you. Did the questions of the Bench raise any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just perhaps a question that may be clarified through an understanding of the particular words.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You had indicated to the Court earlier in your testimony and now today in response to the Court's questions about your brother's membership on the Crisis Staff. And then there was a subsequent -- or there was some discussion about your brother and Mauzer working together, and you indicated they were together on a committee. Sometimes those words, when they're translated back to us, are the same in the B/C/S and different in English, so I'd like to know if -- what committee your brother and Mauzer worked on. Was that the Crisis Staff you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I meant the Crisis Staff at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, by way of a contextual document - I don't have any particular questions about it - I don't believe it's in evidence but I haven't had an ample -- a sufficient opportunity to check, and that's the minutes of the 18th session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly which reflect, among other things, the verification of the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Tuzla, and I can submit some copies of that right now or I could do it at later time but I just wanted to indicate I will be doing so if it's not already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There appears be a bit of confusion. We think now it is, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could do that at the next break so that we can hear from you. Mr. Stewart, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry. Just to clarify something. Excuse me, just to bring up the right day's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: A few minutes ago, Mr. Micic, you said in answer to a question from His Honour Judge Orie about meeting in Belgrade, you said, "I was in touch with the government of Republika Srpska -" that's what it says on the transcript - "with its Ministry for Serbs Outside of Serbia and with a minister of theirs, a certain Mr. Djuretic." Just to clarify, when you say you were in touch with the government of Republika Srpska, is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a misunderstanding. The government of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there are no further questions for you, Mr. Micic, this concludes your testimony in this court. I would like to thank you for coming to The Hague and for answering the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. I wish you a safe trip home again. Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Micic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, I noticed the arrival of Mr. Josse. Does that mean that he will take the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It does mean exactly that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll ask him if he's ready to call his next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I am, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now Madam Usher isn't there. Perhaps meanwhile we can deal with the exhibits. Mr. Registrar. I'll limit myself at this moment to this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D114, Your Honours, the pages from David Owen's book "Balkan Odyssey," undated, pages 246 and 247.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection? Mr. Tieger, any objections against the undated pages of the B/C/S version? I take it apart from a translation is not available at this moment, but apart from that. It's mainly the two maps that were --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. No objection, Your Honour. Translation, I take it, refers to the portions referred to and not anything else that wasn't addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I think as a matter of fact that we will then limit this evidence to the maps and what is under the maps written. So if we could receive translations of the maps and the text under the maps. I think it was 9 and 11 -- 9 and 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1020, Your Honours, the television broadcast with Mr. Micic and Mr. Maksimovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and the next, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1021, the footage on which Mr. Krajisnik appears. P1022, the intercepted conversation between Radovan Karadzic and Momcilo Krajisnik, dated 18 September 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then they are admitted into evidence. We have the translations there. I take it, then, but please verify, that none of the exhibits that was presented to the witness which appears on your list for the tabs, that they're all already in evidence, otherwise I'd like to hear from you, Mr. Tieger. Apart from, of course, the intercepts telephone conversation is under 16. We have dealt with that one. The letter from the Serbian municipality was already in evidence. From what I understand, that was P653, I think it was. That was the letter that appears under tab 18. 46th Assembly session was already in evidence, and then the only one you will still verify is the contextual, and that was the -- the Assembly session. Let me just check. Mr. Tieger, if you could assist me, the last one you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, the minutes of the 18th session of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll verify that, and if it's not yet in evidence, then you'll come back to it so that a number will be assigned to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think, apparently, I can do that now, and I'm told a number needs to be assigned. I don't have 12 copies but I have maybe half a dozen. That's -- if you want me to wait until I have the full set -- I don't know we need a full set, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do it the following way: You give already the one copy to the registrar so that we have the original, which will then be admitted into evidence. It is there in B/C/S and in English, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Prosecution Exhibit P1023 and the translation P1023.1, and that would be for the 18th session Assembly minutes for -- dated the 11th August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stewart, you have had no opportunity yet to look at the documents. Could we proceed on the basis that we admit it into evidence, but if there's any objection, because I never heard any objections against these Assembly minutes, but of course could be, that you have until next Friday to -- to object against it and that otherwise they are provisionally -- they are admitted, and that, Mr. Tieger, you will distribute the copies even today after the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then your next witness, Mr. Josse, would be Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No protective measures. No. Then, Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Pasic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I -- may I just ask Mr. Pasic to leave for one second the courtroom and we'll call you in in one or two minutes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to turn into private session for one second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest to the parties that I confront the witness with the Rule 90(E), but only the first line at this moment. That's saying that if there's a bridge, that we would like the witness to see it and to tell us that there is a bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Pasic. I apologise for having to ask you to leave the courtroom since we were dealing with a procedural matter which took some time. Before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Pasic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I'll invite counsel for the Defence to start his examination, Mr. Pasic, I would like to inform you that if a question is put to you of which you fear your answer might tend to incriminate yourself, that you may address the Chamber and object to answer -- object to answer such a question. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have come here to tell the truth. Independently of what you have just said, I will say what I know about the things that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to inform you that you have the right not to incriminate yourself, and you may then address the Chamber. Mr. Josse, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your name, as we've heard, is Radomir Pasic, and you're from the municipality of Novi Grad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You in fact presently work at the employment office in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Before the first multi-party elections in Bosnia, you worked as a legal officer at the Krajina Promet commercial company in Bosanski Novi?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: I worked as a legal clerk in the company Krajina Promet Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And so that we're all clear - I suspect we are anyway - Bosanski Novi is now known as Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You were a member of the League of Communists, but you were not involved in municipal affairs?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You were a founder member of the SDS in Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: But in fact it wasn't until after the war that you were on the Main Board of that party?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Following the multi-party elections, on the 25th of December of 1990 you became president of the Municipal Assembly of your municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I became the president of the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: There was a significant majority of Serbs within the municipality, and the SDS had a majority in the Municipal Assembly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Nonetheless, the SDS agreed to enter into a power-sharing agreement with the SDA minority?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Dealing with the senior jobs within the municipality, the president of the Executive Committee was also from the SDS, someone called Nikola Omazic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Who was the vice-president of the Municipal Assembly, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: The president of the Municipal Assembly was Sabina Muhamedagic, a lady, on behalf of the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You just said the president of the Municipal Assembly. That wasn't the vice-president -- or she was the vice-president, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Vice-president. If I said president, it was a slip of the tongue. I meant vice-president. The vice-president of the Municipal Assembly was Sabina Muhamedagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And she was a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And the SDA also were awarded with the vice-presidency of the Executive Committee?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And the name of the occupant of that office was what, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR PASIC
utterances.text: Nijaz Kapetanovic. I think his surname was Kapetanovic. Nijaz was his first name, and I think Kapetanovic was his surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
